ANA.head: We gave Anaheim a 66% chance, and they delivered.

CGY.head: We gave Calgary only a 34% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: The Ducks run away from the Flames
paras: Jeff Malott opened the scoring for the Ducks a little over a minute in. Cutter Gauthier made it 2-0 midway through the first, with Tyson Hinds picking up his first NHL point on the goal. The Ducks scored four times in the third. Tim Washe stretched the lead to 3-0 early in the third, but Mikael Backlund got the Flames on the board less than two minutes later. Beckett Sennecke made it 4-1 for the Ducks 25 seconds later. He scored his second of the night into the empty net with less than four minutes left. Mikael Granlund pushed the lead to 6-1, 52 seconds later. Sennecke added an assist for a three-point night.

The Ducks carried the play, outshooting the Flames 34-21, and got the result to match. Ville Husso, who gave up seven goals against Buffalo in his last start, made 20 saves for the Ducks, and Devin Cooley stopped 28 of 33 at the other end. The Ducks improved to 11-9-1, third in the Pacific, while the Flames dropped to 9-11-1, sixth in the Pacific.

items.text: Cutter Gauthier has a point in eleven straight games, with a goal in each of the last nine.
Leo Carlsson’s seven-game point streak against Calgary ended.
The Ducks bounced back after two straight losses.
NHL.com had projected the Ducks with 12 forwards and six defensemen, but they dressed 11 and seven.
